title: Duplicate responses & token loss — customer status + follow-up draft
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for external-facing communications after the event that caused duplicate completion responses and occasional token loss for a subset of API requests. Use this to populate the status page entry and to craft an email to affected enterprise integrations.

Audience:
- Primary: API customers with heavy streaming or long-sequence workloads (>=2048 tokens).
- Secondary: internal account and solutions teams who will field customer questions.

Short status (one-liner for status page):
We observed duplicated completion responses and intermittent token trimming for some requests between 2027-08-06 23:40 UTC and 2027-08-07 01:10 UTC. The root cause has been identified and mitigations implemented; a full data and behavior review is in progress.

Current customer-facing summary (ready-to-publish):
What happened: For a limited set of API requests, clients received duplicated final responses (duplicate completions) or responses missing trailing tokens. This was most apparent for streaming sessions and long prompt+completion combinations.
Impact: Affected requests were approx. 0.6% of total traffic during the window and skewed to a small set of enterprise customers that run long-context generation or aggressive client-side streaming. No customer data was exposed beyond each request; no authentication or credential compromise.
What we did: We throttled a misbehaving routing path and deployed a fix to the streaming relay library that ensures single-terminal write semantics and stronger KV-cache boundaries. This stopped new duplicates and reduced token trimming within 20 minutes of rollout.
Next steps: We will run a replay analysis on stored request traces to quantify affected outputs, provide remediation guidance to customers, and publish a concise technical root-cause update within 72 hours.

Suggested status page timeline entry (short format):
- 2027-08-06 23:40 UTC — Anomalous duplicate completions and token truncation first detected in streaming telemetry.
- 2027-08-06 23:55 UTC — Initial mitigation: limited routing change to isolate relay path.
- 2027-08-07 00:02 UTC — Hotfix deployed to streaming-relay library (v1.18.4).
- 2027-08-07 00:22 UTC — Duplicate and trimming signals returned to baseline.
- 2027-08-10 01:30 UTC — Detailed root cause post (technical) to be published.

Draft email to affected customers (concise):
Subject: Brief update — Observed duplicated responses / truncated tokens (Aug 6 UTC)
Hi <Customer Name>,
We wanted to let you know we observed an issue impacting a subset of API requests on Aug 6 between 23:40–01:10 UTC where some streaming sessions received duplicated final responses or responses missing trailing tokens. We have deployed a fix and isolated the routing path that introduced the behavior.
We are currently replaying request traces to identify affected outputs and will follow up with specifics and remediation options (replay/export or targeted re-run) within 72 hours. If you prefer we do this work for you, reply and we’ll coordinate with your engineering contact.
Apologies for the disruption — we know deterministic completions are important and we are prioritizing this.
— Lena (Redwood Inference Customer Success)

Longer customer technical note (for enterprise integrations):
Technical summary (non-sensitive): During normal traffic routing, an edge relay was inadvertently re-queuing a partially finalized frame when an adjacent worker signaled completion concurrently. That re-queue produced a second terminal write to the client stream in a small number of cases. Separately, an off-by-one in the relay's token-merge path could discard the last buffer chunk when reordering happened across two batches, resulting in missing trailing tokens.
Why this affected you more: Customers with long sequence lengths and client libraries that rely on exact terminal token alignment (streaming clients that close on EOF) saw duplicates or truncated endings more often.
Mitigation and fix: We applied a conservative in-flight deduplication for terminal frames at the relay and corrected the token-merge off-by-one. Unit and integration tests were added to cover concurrent completion and reorder scenarios.
Data retention and privacy: No request payloads were exfiltrated. Replay analysis will be done against logs and traces retained under our usual retention policy; we will not export or share request payloads without customer consent.

Customer Q&A (anticipated):
Q: Will you re-run the affected requests for me?
A: We can offer a replay service for customers with confirmed impact. Reply to this thread to coordinate. For customers on Dedicated or Private, we will provide tooling to run replays in your environment if desired.

Q: How many responses were duplicated?
A: Initial sampling shows ~0.6% requests with either duplicate terminal writes or trailing token loss in the window. We’ll provide per-customer counts in the follow-up.

Q: Are there any changes we must make on our side?
A: Recommended short-term mitigations for streaming clients:
- Treat duplicate terminal frames as idempotent (ignore exact-duplicate final messages).
- Re-validate client-side EOF detection to avoid closing on partial frames.
We will publish a small client-library patch for official SDKs within 48 hours.

Internal action items (owners):
- SRE: finalize replay analysis and share per-customer affected counts (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2027-08-11 18:00 UTC).
- Serving runtime: merge and ship additional integration tests for concurrent completion (owner: Devon Li, PR linked).
- Solutions Eng / CSM: prepare individual outreach for top 10 affected accounts and offer replays (owner: Aisha Khan, due: 2027-08-11 EOD).
- Legal / Compliance: validate no regulatory reporting required for targeted customers in regulated sectors (owner: Priya Sharma, due: 2027-08-12).

Internal notes / things to watch (working):
- Check whether similar relay path exists in Dedicated clusters and apply patch there if present.
- Verify billing token counts for affected requests; correct any billing anomalies if traced to truncation.
- Ensure status page link is added to the ticket and to the customer-facing email.

Draft longer post-incident technical write-up (outline):
1) Executive summary + impact numbers (per-region, per-customer buckets)
2) Timeline (detection, mitigations, fix deploys)
3) Deep technical cause (relay concurrency + token-merge off-by-one)
4) Test coverage gaps and what we added
5) Customer remediation paths and tooling we built
6) Follow-ups (SLA credit review, SDK patch schedule)

To-do before publishing:
- Confirm wording with legal and privacy.
- Add any regulatory-required disclosures for European financial customers.
- Attach per-customer counts only after SRE verification.
- Prepare SDK patch and link in the post.

Notes to self: keep tone apologetic but factual; avoid technical minutiae on the status page (reserve for postmortem). Coordinate the follow-up timing so customers get the per-account numbers and remediation options in the same communication.

Revision history:
- 2027-08-09 initial draft (Lena)
- 2027-08-10 added owner assignments and linked PRs (Marco)

---
End of draft.
